messages:
Ravi Patel: Hi team — had an ER visit in Lisbon last night after a fall. I left my wallet at the hospital and only have a brief paper receipt with no NIF/tax id. I need to submit for reimbursement and also to get a temporary ID card. What do you need?

People Ops: Oh no, hope you're ok. For reimbursements we need an itemized invoice and proof of payment. If the hospital won't provide a tax id (NIF), we accept a signed provider attestation on letterhead. Please upload photos to the portal.

Ravi Patel: I only have a small receipt that lists "Atendimento Urgente" and total EUR 420. No NIF, just hospital stamp and date. I paid by card  I have the card txn screenshot.

Claims Team: Checklist to upload under "Travel & Foreign":
- Photo of receipt (line items visible if possible)
- Card transaction screenshot showing amount and date
- Short English translation of receipt lines
- Provider attestation if no NIF (signed by hospital)

Claims Team: If the hospital can provide an itemized bill within 30 days we can use that. Otherwise attestation + receipt + card txn is sufficient for intake. Reimbursement is in USD using the FX rate on the service date.

Ravi Patel: Uploaded receipt_lisbon.jpg and card_txn.jpg and translation.txt. Also, hospital said they can email a signed attestation to claims@redwood.com if we provide the claim ref.

People Ops: Thanks. Use subject: "Reimbursement Request  Ravi Patel  Lisbon ER  Claim 1934567890" when asking hospital to email. We can also issue a temporary digital ID card valid for 30 days for pharmacy/hospital use. Want us to generate that and email you a PDF?

Ravi Patel: Yes please for the digital ID. Email to ravi.patel@redwood.com. And please include a phone number the hospital can call to verify.

Benefits Bot: Reminder: upload via benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "Travel & Foreign" for fastest processing. Attach translation file if receipt not in English.

People Ops: Digital temporary ID created and emailed (ID-193456-AUTO). It redacts the full policy number and includes benefits verification line + phone + claims email. Also uploaded a template message you can forward to the hospital to request the signed attestation.

Ravi Patel: Hospital replied they will send attestation to claims@redwood.com with subject as you suggested. Anything else I should expect?

Claims Team: Expect intake confirmation within 48 hours of receiving the attestation. Full adjudication 7-14 business days after all docs. If hospital invoices directly to us and we accept, we can handle payment; otherwise we'll reimburse you in USD. We'll post the estimated USD amount after conversion.

Luisa Martins: FYI when I had ER in Portugal they asked for the hospital stam pphoto and a quick police report for ambulance calls. If you used an ambulance and have any police docs upload them too.

Ravi Patel: I didn't use ambulance. No police report. Thanks for the help — will ping if hospital asks for anything else.

Benefits Bot: Tip: Keep a photo of your digital ID and receipts in the portal for faster claims when traveling.
